shortDescription: Generate, update, and optionally write Kubernetes kubeconfig files

options.name: clusters
options.description: List of cluster definitions to merge into the kubeconfig. Each cluster is identified by its C(name). When C(name) matches an existing cluster, the default C(behavior) is V(merge). See the C(behavior) suboption for V(replace), V(keep), and V(remove).

options.name: contexts
options.description: List of context definitions linking users and clusters. Each context is identified by its C(name). When C(name) matches an existing context, the default C(behavior) is V(merge). See the C(behavior) suboption for V(replace), V(keep), and V(remove).

options.name: current_context
options.description: Name of the context to set as current/active. This context will be used by default when using kubectl. Must match one of the context names defined in O(contexts).

options.name: dest
options.description: Destination path where the final kubeconfig should be written. If not specified, the kubeconfig will be saved to O(path). Allows copying and modifying a kubeconfig to a new location.

options.name: path
options.description: Path to an existing kubeconfig file to load and merge from. If the file does not exist, a new kubeconfig will be created. This becomes the default destination if O(dest) is not specified.

options.name: preferences
options.description: Kubeconfig preferences. Used for client-side settings like color output, default editor, etc.

options.name: users
options.description: List of user authentication configurations. Each user is identified by its C(name). When C(name) matches an existing user, the default C(behavior) is V(merge). See the C(behavior) suboption for V(replace), V(keep), and V(remove).
